segments.narration: A whole town reported being gassed by nobody. Mattoon, Illinois, 1944, more than two dozen cases and not one attacker.
It ran from the thirty-first of August to the thirteenth of September. The first call came from a man named Urban Raef.
The accounts matched closely. A sweet smell at the window, then coughing, nausea, legs that would not hold weight.
Armed men patrolled the streets. By the twelfth of September the police chief said plainly there had probably been no attacks at all.
Industrial fumes drifting in, and fear doing the rest. A 1945 psychology paper made Mattoon the textbook case of mass hysteria.
